question: Can the current automatic-mask concerns be turned into explicit outer-field drafts for substantive source-bound review?
scope: Eight native outer-field geometry proposals, both BOI signs; no detector, adoption, source write, frame exclusion or window approval.
evidence: Existing 021 five fixed-frame sheets and source native coordinates. Prior 023 automatic maps were seen; drafting is not blinded. No matched anatomical reference has been established by this task.

method.draft: One manually estimated polygon per recording. No holes, intensity segmentation, component removal or interpolation across excluded frames.
method.rasterization: MATLAB inpolygon on native pixel centers (column,row) = 1..512; polygon boundary included. Acquisition boundaries at 0.5/512.5 retain edge pixels.
method.review: Existing reviewBOITissueSupport produces ProposedMask.mat, Proposal.json and first/middle/last previews. Additional five-fixed-frame overlays mark uncertain segments orange; no adoption writer called.
method.comparison: Source-bound draft versus preserved 023 automatic masks: retained/added/removed pixels, sink/surge areas and nominal area-time only. Do not infer changed event outcomes using old numerators.
method.timing: External exact 1 Hz; full nominal source extent only. Established pre-recording state, interval unmeasured. No inferred induction or experimental baseline.
method.uncertainty: Per-file boundary uncertainty and numbered uncertain segments are review annotations, not statistical confidence intervals. ID402 iso all segments are uncertain.

verification: Independent native pixel-center polygon replay, connected/hole-free geometry, interior-retention points, default sink border, both sign areas, proposal/source hashes and prior artifact preservation.
stopping_rule: One initial draft set. Revise only a documented coordinate/rendering error or explicit source-based boundary review; do not revise to achieve an area or expected state difference.
